items.summary: Advance C13-BLUEPRINT-CONVERGENCE from planned with exact evidence
notes: Nothing built today discriminates convergence from the idempotence C13-BLUEPRINT-REMATERIALIZE already verifies. Its selector proves re-applying one unchanged Blueprint reconciles to a semantic no-op, which is f(f(x)) = f(x) for one input; path-independence needs a differential harness that applies one Blueprint to a Scope by at least two admissible issue orders and from at least two different prior managed states, then asserts one identical Blueprint-managed record set once the pending set is empty. An implementation that reached the declared state only from an empty Scope must fail it

The pending set has to be carried by the reconciliation outcome rather than computed alongside it, so that converged is that set being empty rather than a separate report a host can get wrong. Verification requires the outcome type to hold the obligations and a mutation that states convergence while an obligation stands to break a cited test; a boolean flag set next to a nonempty obligation list satisfies the prose and must not satisfy the atom

Each of the four stated deferrals needs its own obligation-shape evidence — record, reason, and discharging condition all named: a reliance hold under C13-FACET-DEPENDENCY-ORDER, each draining Invocation item under C13-FACET-WITHDRAWAL-DRAIN, each unadmitted RouteReservation terminalized by a rejected RouteDelivery, and a Package retained under SPEC 5.2. The rejected-reconciliation clause is what stops converging from becoming an excuse, so it needs the strongest negative evidence: a divergence expressible as no pending obligation — a withdrawal set the host cannot compute, or a retired Slot declaration still holding an entry attributed to a retained Facet — must be refused at validation before package code loads, on the no-code-loaded terms C13-BLUEPRINT-VALIDATE-BEFORE-LOAD already tests, and must never be admitted and left pending

items.summary: Advance C13-CLOUDFLARE-AUTHORITY-PERMIT-BINDING from implemented with exact evidence
notes: The unforgeable target-bound capability now exists. TargetBoundTenantAuthority is minted by the Tenant for one exact caller ActorRef, takes no caller argument on any method, and stamps that identity on every forwarded call, so a holder cannot answer for another Actor by editing a payload. The payload itself stays opaque in this profile: SPEC section 10.3 places the issuance decision in the Tenant, so the capability carries bytes and authenticates who sent them and decides nothing about them.

Duplicate and response-loss semantics are held rather than emulated. A repeat of one idempotency key with byte-identical content is forwarded again, because the Tenant's own permit record is the single source of truth for whether it already issued and answering in transit would be a second durable copy of an authority decision; a repeat with different bytes is refused before the Tenant sees it, because it would ask one nonce to bind two requests. The guard retains one canonical digest per key rather than the payload, because both the key and the payload are attacker-supplied and a guard that grows with what a holder sends is memory exhaustion inside a 128 MB isolate rather than a safety check. Three bounds hold it, each declared once and each tested at the exact value it admits and the first value it refuses: MAXIMUM_KEYED_CALLS distinct keys per capability, MAXIMUM_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_LENGTH characters per key, and SQL_BLOB_LIMIT_BYTES per payload. Every refusal is proven to occur before the sink, by a recording sink whose call count does not move, and an over-limit payload is proven not to consume a distinct-key slot either. A lost response is exercised end to end: the Tenant issues, the target admits nothing, the retry replays that exact issuance, and the admission happens once.

The seven approved core boundary symbols are now public on the authority and protocol subpaths and remain forbidden on the root package. The packed consumer verifies those exact surfaces, and the real-workerd permit lane exercises the composed path without re-implementing any authority decision in this profile.

Deployed evidence is still owed for the third clause. On workerd 1.20260708.1 the Tenant capability's RpcTarget disposer runs after the client execution context ends, so final release cannot be observed inside this hermetic lane. The lane proves that releasing the original handle does not sever its duplicate. The structural capability test proves refusal after the final local release, and the Tenant exposes a release count for a live lane that outlives one request.

items.summary: Advance C13-TURN-HANDLE-DETACHMENT from implemented with exact evidence
notes: Publication is now the commit point in the durable sense as well as the logical one, and the two commit points §5.6 describes are two construction paths rather than one. TurnAdmissionVerifier.admit builds an Invocation-identity handle over an AdmittedInvocationItem — invocation, item index, item key and the exact EffectAttempt — and reads no Receipt at all, which is what a detached admission leaves behind. A child RunRef handle keeps the Receipt-based path, because a child reference exists only once the delegate Receipt carries it; the spawn Receipt and its result digest moved onto that identity case, so an Invocation identity has no field they could occupy.

TurnAdmissionPublisher.publish reserves the Run obligation and appends the Invocation owner's admission message in one Run transaction, and RunRuntime.terminalizeRunInTransaction appends one cancellation message per still-owed published item in the same transition that terminalizes the Run. A response lost after that transaction commits loses no command: RunRuntime.pendingInvocationDeliveries replays each message after a restart, and RunRuntime.acknowledgeInvocationDelivery discharges it idempotently with no caller-supplied revision, because an owner whose acknowledgement response was lost knows no current revision.

The Run ships no §7.4 verdict, and has no field for one. TurnAdmissionHandle.cancelledBy and RunTerminalization.cancelled are deleted rather than deprecated: the Run observed its own end, not whether cancellation reached a live target controller, and after a restart there is no controller left to reach. What the Run owes is a request naming the exact attempt; the Invocation owner's target aborts the controller keyed by that attempt and the existing AttemptFailureKind.classify path derives `aborted` from what the target observed, while an absent controller leaves the outcome indeterminate for reconciliation.

The prohibition on the issuing Turn's cancellation reaching a published item holds by identity: TextId compares its constructor, so a published item's owner, always a RunId, never equals a cancelled TurnId. An item no Turn published is reached by neither scope, which is C13-FACET-CANCELLATION-REACH's rule and not this one's.

Which handles a Run cancellation can address is decided by the item's Receipt state, not by the method that built the handle, and the distinction matters for anyone reading this row. cancellationDeliveriesInTransaction skips an item whose current Receipt is terminal before it resolves the handle at all. TurnAdmissionVerifier.verify returns only on the succeeded evidence shape, and a succeeded AttemptReceipt is terminal, so a verify-built handle is never addressed in a truthful state; §7.4 admits supersession only of `indeterminate`, which that path never accepts, so the gate cannot open. An admit-built handle names an attempt no Receipt names yet, so it is addressed until its own Receipt lands.

That argument rests on one host-supplied premise, stated here rather than hidden: invocationItemTerminal is a predicate on the abstract SettlementEvidencePort, and the runtime trusts it. A host that answered it untruthfully would address an item that already has a Receipt. Even then no second Receipt is written, because the Invocation owner's cancellation path re-reads its own state and reports the item settled before it asks the target.

items.summary: Advance C13-VIEW-WITHDRAWAL-TERMINAL from implemented with exact evidence
notes: A View stream is now the pair of a SurfaceId and the SurfaceEpoch its registration assigned. View carries the terminal field and ViewDelta carries the epoch, both at bumped codec majors with no reader left for the previous ones. Retirement emits exactly one terminal ViewDelta whose cursor is the base View's own, because that patch consumes no Event, and every later snapshot or delta for that epoch is refused by reading the terminal View rather than a second liveness flag.

An epoch belongs to a registration rather than to a retirement. WorkspacePersistence requires a current SurfaceRegistration for the exact SurfaceId before a stream opens and before any revision advances, so retirement alone cannot open epoch 2 and only a reinstallation can. currentSurfaceEpoch derives the next epoch from the stored Views, which compaction cannot delete for a retired epoch, so a later PackagePin registering the same static SurfaceId opens a fresh stream at the next epoch while every earlier terminal View stays readable at the revision it ended on.

Resume is keyed on the opaque EventCursor the record defines, not on a revision a client would have to derive. ViewReplayProtocol.replay resolves a presented cursor against the stored Views and deltas of that exact stream, refuses an unknown cursor and a cursor of another stream by name, and yields a retired epoch's terminal revision through the same reader live resume uses. A client detects retirement from the returned View alone, holding no live handle.
